FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Organic 
Chemicals, Alcohols and Allied Products Sectional Committee had been approved by the Petroleum, Coal and 
Related Products Division Council. 


Octylphenol is an organic chemical with molecular formula C14H220. Other common names of Octylphenol are 
4-octylphenol, 4-tert-octylphenol, p-tert-octylphenol and p-(t-octyl) phenol. 


OH 


CgH17 


Molecular formula : C14H20 


Molecular weight : 206.32 


In general, the term ‘Octylphenol’ represents a large number of isomeric compounds of the general formula 
CgH17.C6H4(OH). The octyl group (СНз) may be branched in a variety of ways or be a straight chain (like in 4- 
n-octylphenol) and may be located at either the 2-, 3- or 4-position of the benzene ring. Of these potential isomers, 
4-tert-octylphenol (CAS No. 140-66-9) is the most commercially important and is one of the important major 
constituents in the mixture of commercial ‘Octylphenol’. 


Octylphenol is a highly used chemical, mainly as an intermediate in the production of phenol/formaldehyde resins 
(98 percent of use) and in the manufacture of octylphenol ethoxylates (2 percent use). 


A small amount of the ethoxylates is used to produce ether sulphates. The end uses from the manufacture of these 
resins, ethoxylates and ether sulphates are various [for example, a tackifier in rubber for tyres, water-based paints, 
pesticide formulations (as a dispersant) etc.], but the extent to which octylphenol reaches the environment from 
such products is not clear. It is also reported that octylphenol is present as an impurity in commercial grade 
nonylphenol and this may account to some extent for its detection in the environment. 


Octylphenol, is toxic to aquatic life. It is an endocrine disruptor with estrogenic activity, and thus it is considered 
to be a risk particularly for freshwater and marine aquatic animals. 


Based on the recommendations of Department of Chemicals and Petrochemicals, Ministry of Chemicals and 
Fertilizer, the Committee has decided to formulate Indian Standard on of 4-octylphenol. 


The composition of the Committee, responsible for the formulation of this standard is given at Annex B. 


For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with the final value, 
observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 
2022 ‘Rules for rounding off numerical values (second revision)’. The number of significant places retained in 
the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

Indian Standard 


4-OCTYLPHENOL (4 -tert-OCTYLPHENOL) — 
SPECIFICATION 


1 SCOPE 


This standard prescribes the requirements, the 
methods of sampling and testing of 4-octylphenol 
(4-tert-octylphenol). 


2 REFERENCES 


The following standards contain provisions which, 
through reference in this text, constitute provisions 
of this standard. At the time of publication, the 
editions indicated were valid. All standards are 
subject to revision and parties to agreements based 
on this standard are encouraged to investigate the 
possibility of applying the most recent editions of 
the standards given below:

cobalt scale (second revision) 


3 REQUIREMENTS 
3.1 Description 


The material shall be in the form of crystalline 
powder, bulk (molten liquid) or flakes. 


3.2 The material shall also comply with the 
requirements given in Table 1, when tested 
according to the methods prescribed in col 4 and col 
5 of the Table 1.

4 PACKING AND MARKING 
4.1 Packing 


The material shall be packaged in а suitable 
polypropylene coated 25 kg paper bag or super sack 
made of polypropylene or as agreed to between the 
purchaser and the supplier. Each package shall be 
securely closed. 


4.2 Marking 


4.2.1 Each package shall bear legibly and indelibly 
the following information: 


a) Name of the material; 

b) Name of manufacturer and his recognized 
trade-mark, if any; 

c) Net mass of material; 

d) Month and year of the manufacture; 

e) Batch or lot number; and 

f) Any other statutory requirements. 


4.2.2 BIS Certification Marking 


The product(s) conforming to the requirements of 
this standard may be certified as per the conformity 
assessment schemes under the provisions of the 
Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 and the Rules 
and Regulations framed thereunder, апа Ше 
products may be marked with the standard mark. 


5 SAMPLING 


5.1 The method of drawing representative samples 
of the material shall be drawn as prescribed in 4 of 
IS 5299. 


5.2 Numbers of Tests 


5.2.1 Tests for the determination of assay and ortho- 
tert-octylphenol shall be conducted оп the 
individual samples. 


5.2.2 Tests for the determination of remaining 
characteristics, namely, description, colour, phenol 
content and moisture content shall be conducted on 
the composite sample. 


5.3 Criteria for Conformity 
5.3.1 For Individual Samples 


The batch shall be declared as conforming to the 
requirement of assay and ortho-tert-octylphenol, if 
each of the individual test results satisfies the 
relevant requirements given in Table 1. 


5.3.2 For Composite Sample 


For declaring the conformity of the lot to the 
requirements of all other characteristics (see 5.2.2) 
tested on the composite sample, the test results for 
each of the characteristics shall satisfy the relevant 
requirements given in 3 and Table 1. 


6 TEST METHODS 


6.1 Tests shall be carried out according to the 
methods referred in col 4 and col 5 of Table 1. 


6.2 Quality of Reagents 


Unless specified otherwise, ‘pure chemicals’ and 
distilled water (see IS 1070) shall be employed in 
tests. 


NOTE — ‘Pure chemicals’ shall mean chemicals that 
do not contain impurities which affect the results of 
analysis. 


IS 17940 : 2022 


ANNEX A 
[Table 1, SI No. (ii), (iii) and (iv)] 


DETERMINATION OF 4-tert-OCTYLPHENOL CONTENT AND ITS IMPURITIES (ASSAY) BY GAS 
CHROMATOGRAPHY (GC) 


A-1 OUTLINE OF METHOD 


This procedure is used to determine assay of 4-tert- 
octylphenol (PTOP). Capillary Gas 
Chromatography is used to determine the percentage 
of PTOP and its impurities. Quantitative results are 
achieved through direct area percent normalization. 
The major impurities assayed by this procedure are 
some unknown impurities, phenol, and Ortho-tert- 
octylphenol (OTOP). 


A-2 APPARATUS 
A-2.1 Gas Chromatograph 


Any gas chromatograph equipped with a flame 
ionization detector (FID), a split-splitless injector 


A-2.1.3 Injection port information, as given below 


and a suitable electronic integrator/software can be 
used with following accessories and operating 
condition. 


A-2.1.1 Column 


Capillary column with (5 percent-phenyl)- 
methylpolysiloxane nonpolar phase with 30 m 
length, 0.32 mm internal diameter, 1.0 um film 
thickness and 320°C maximum temperature or 
equivalent column 


A-2.1.2 Carrier gas, nitrogen grade 5.0 (purity 
99.999 percent).

A-3 PROCEDURE 


Take 0.050 g + 0.01 g of sample and add 20 ml to 
vial. Now add 10 ml of acetone (HPLC grade) to vial 
by pipet. Shake the vial to completely dissolve the 
content. Inject 1.0 pl. Run the chromatogram. 
Calculate the percentage composition by area 
normalization with response factor 1.00. 


A-4 CALCULATION 


Take value of 4-tert-octylphenol and its impurities 
by percent area normalization method.

Review of Indian Standards 


Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the website-
